email.body1:
Rhegan, saw Cirrus widening ScreenHub and your AI signage lines across automotive, retail, education and restaurants on the subscription model.

Covering that many verticals usually means more in-market accounts than the team can touch, and good-fit prospects go cold before a rep reaches them. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Cirrus off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing those progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Rhegan, quick follow-up for Cirrus.

A multi-vertical, subscription motion makes pipeline coverage hard to pin down. Most teams don't actually know how many meetings they need to book to hit target, so the gap surfaces late and the quarter turns into a scramble while reps drown in research.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I'll walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Cirrus needs to close that gap this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Rhegan, last bit of proof for Cirrus.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Cirrus's reply rate likely compares to other B2B software teams. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?
email.body4:
Rhegan, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling pipeline without adding headcount isn't a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Timing matters, and running a multi-vertical signage motion keeps a sales manager busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your motion? I'll tailor it to Cirrus either way.
